subject: Post-trial visibility add-ons — conversion scenarios & billing model walkthrough
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara@cloudwave.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudwave.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial wrap — visibility add-ons questions

Hi David,

Thanks for the trial — our engineering team liked the dashboard views and trace retention, but procurement asked me to get concrete scenarios before we convert. Two quick asks: 1) examples of how billing would look if we keep 30 days vs 90 days retention for traces and dashboards (we're currently on the 30-day trial defaults), and 2) whether you offer an overage crediting mechanism if we spike above our committed slab during an event window.

We expect the service to go into production mid-October and want to model costs for FY27. If you can share sample invoices or a simple simulation (CSV) that would help. Also copy me on any commercial levers (pilot credits, transient discounts) your team can provide for conversion.

Appreciate it —
Sara
Sara Liu
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudWave

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial wrap — visibility add-ons questions

Sara —

Thanks for the clear asks. I've attached a short proposal and a CSV with three billing scenarios: baseline (30d retention), extended (90d retention with tiered archival), and event-window (30d retention + short-term surge to 180d for 72 hours). High-level notes below and a recommended commercial path. Ben & Marissa are looped for credits and packaging options.

Quick summary (full numbers in the attached CSV):
- 30d baseline: predictable slab pricing, no archival surcharge; estimated $4.8k/mo for current ingestion profile.
- 90d extended: ~1.6x token/storage cost vs 30d; recommended to pick this if you need longer investigation windows. We model a 45% incremental cost mostly from longtail object storage.
- Event-window: short-term surge reserved as a billed spike with a built-in 50% partial-credit if average monthly usage returns below committed slab within 2 billing cycles. This avoids heavy upfront reserved capacity for occasional incidents.

Commercial levers we can offer for a first-year conversion:
- Pilot conversion credit: one month of retention fees waived for first 3 months after signing (applies to add-ons).
- Volume step credits: ramp credits at 3, 6, 12 month marks tied to actual token ingestion.
- Overage smoothing: we can apply a 50% overage credit for up to two non-consecutive spikes in a 12-month period on the extended retention SKU.

Ben, Marissa — can you confirm the standard language we use for the 50% overage credit (term, limits, and whether it appears on the invoice as a credit line or a separate rebate post-invoice)?

Sara — I'll follow up with a short call this afternoon if that works to walk the CSV and the attached one-pager.

—David
David Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara@cloudwave.com>, procurement@cloudwave.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 13:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial wrap — visibility add-ons questions

Quick reply on the crediting mechanics so David can finalize the proposal copy:

We normally implement the 50% overage "smoothing" as an invoice-level credit applied in the billing cycle following the spike. Key points:
- Credit triggers: single-day peak > 3x committed slab OR 7-day rolling avg > 1.5x committed slab.
- Maximum: up to two spikes per 12-month period.
- Documentation: we include a short addendum to SOW that spells trigger thresholds and credit amount; credits appear as an invoice credit line (reduces amount due).
- We only allow smoothing on extended retention SKUs (90d) or on the event-window product when customers have a minimum 3-month conversion credit active.

For CloudWave specifically, I recommend: 1) 90d retention with an event-window buffer (72h) and 25% pilot credit applied to first three invoices. That keeps us protected on margin while giving them runway.

Marissa — can you draft the brief addendum (2–3 bullets) that spells the trigger and credit display on invoice? I'll include it in the proposal PDF.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara@cloudwave.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial wrap — visibility add-ons questions

Sara — attaching a one-paragraph addendum we can slot into the SOW and the proposal. Also included the proposal PDF and a CSV with the line-item simulations you requested.

On invoice presentation: we will show the overage smoothing as a separate "Smoothing Credit" line under adjustments. The credit posts in the billing cycle after the spike has been validated (we run a 3-business-day validation window to rule out instrumentation noise).

SOW addendum (text):
"Overage smoothing: In the event of an operational spike meeting the agreed trigger thresholds (single-day peak > 3x committed slab OR 7-day rolling average > 1.5x committed slab), Redwood Inference will apply a smoothing credit equal to 50% of the overage charge for up to two qualifying spikes in any rolling 12-month period. Credits will be displayed as an invoice credit under 'Smoothing Credit' once validated. The customer must be on the Extended Retention SKU or have an active event-window buffer product to be eligible."

Next steps: if this looks good to you, Sara — can we lock a 30-minute call tomorrow 9:00am PT to run the CSV and the proposal? If procurement needs a separate DocuSign, I can route that as well.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
